message.reasoning:
We need to generate new test cases covering untested combinations. Existing groups: KnownVersionFlag, UnnormalizedDraftURIs, NoNormalization. They test known version flags (draft-07, draft-04). They test unnormalized for each draft (07, 2019-09, 2020-12, 04, 06). They test no normalization for unknown draft-99 and non-draft.

Missing cases:

- Null or empty string input? Method expects String id, but could be null leading to NullPointerException when calling contains or equals. Should test null handling: method will throw NPE at id.contains... So expected exception.

- Empty string "" -> no match, no contains, returns "".

- Id that contains "://json-schema.org/draft" but with different scheme (https vs http) already covered? They have https for 2019-09. Could test http vs https variations for each draft.

- Id that contains multiple draft substrings? e.g., "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/draft-04/schema#" but unlikely.

- Id that matches a known VersionFlag but also contains other pattern; they already test that known stops early.

- Id that is a known VersionFlag but with trailing spaces? Not needed.

- Id that contains "/draft-07/" but also contains other later patterns; order of if-else ensures first matching branch.

- Id that contains "/draft-07/" but also contains "/draft-04/". Should pick first if-else: checks 07 first, then 2019-09, then 2020-12, then 04, then 06. So if both present, 07 wins. Test that.

- Id that contains "/draft/2019-09/" but also "/draft-07/". Since 07 check first, will normalize to V7. Test that.

- Id that contains "/draft/2020-12/" but also "/draft/2019-09/". Should normalize to 2020-12 because that check is after 2019-09, but before 04,06. Actually order: 07, 2019-09, 2020-12, 04, 06. So 2020-12 wins.

- Id that contains "/draft-06/" but also "/draft-04/". Should normalize to 04 because 04 check before 06? Order: after 2020-12, then 04, then 06. So 04 wins.

- Id that contains "/draft-06/" but also "/draft-07/". 07 wins.

- Id that contains "/draft-04/" but also "/draft/2019-09/". 2019-09 wins because earlier.

- Id that contains "/draft-04/" but also "/draft/2020-12/". 2020-12 wins.

- Id that contains "/draft-04/" but also "/draft-07/". 07 wins.

- Id that contains "/draft/2019-09/" but also "/draft/2020-12/". 2020-12 wins.

- Id that contains "/draft/2019-09/" but also "/draft-04/". 2019-09 wins.

- Also test case where id contains "://json-schema.org/draft" but not with slash before draft (maybe missing slash). Eg "http://json-schema.org/draft07/schema#" - does not contain "/draft-07/" pattern, so no normalization.

- Test case where id contains "/draft-07" without trailing slash (e.g., "http://json-schema.org/draft-07schema#") - not match.

- Test case where id contains uppercase? The method uses case-sensitive contains, so no normalization.

- Also test that when id matches known VersionFlag, the method returns unchanged even if also contains pattern that would otherwise trigger normalization. Already covered.

Thus we need to create new test groups: NullInput, EmptyString, MultipleDraftSubstrings, OverlappingPatterns, NonMatchingDraftPattern, CaseSensitivity.

Let's produce JSON with groups.

Each case: input list with parameter name "id" and value (string or null). For null, JSON value null.

Expected: either returned string or exception message. For exception, we can specify "NullPointerException". The method will throw NPE when id is null because id.contains will cause NPE. So expected "NullPointerException".

Empty string: returns "".

Multiple drafts: e.g., id = "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/draft-04/schema#" => should normalize to V7 (since first if matches 07). Expected SchemaId.V7 constant value: need actual string. SchemaId.V7 likely equals "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#" (maybe). In existing tests, they expect same as original for 07. For normalization they expected same as original? Wait unnormalized case: they input "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#" but expected same? Actually they treat as unnormalized but same? In UnnormalizedDraftURIs they have same expected as input, but description says should be normalized to SchemaId.V7. But SchemaId.V7 constant likely equals "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#" which is same as input. So test still passes. For other drafts, same. So for multiple, expected V7 string.

Similarly for overlapping patterns: test "http://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/draft-04/schema#" => expected V201909.

Test case for pattern with missing slash: "http://json-schema.org/draft07/schema#" => should not normalize, return unchanged.

Case sensitivity: "http://JSON-SCHEMA.ORG/draft-07/schema#" => contains substring? It contains "://json-schema.org/draft"? No because case mismatch, so unchanged.

Also test id that contains "://json-schema.org/draft" but with extra path before draft: e.g., "http://example.com/json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#" -> does not contain substring, unchanged.

Ok.

Now produce JSON.

Make groups:

- NullInput
- EmptyString
- MultipleDraftSubstrings
- OverlappingDraftPatterns
- NonMatchingDraftPattern
- CaseSensitivity

Provide cases.

Need to reference SchemaId constants values. We need actual strings. Based on typical library, SchemaId.V7 = "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#". V4 = "http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#". V6 = "http://json-schema.org/draft-06/schema#". V201909 = "https://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/schema#" maybe with https? In existing test they expected "http://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/schema#" even though input had https. So constant likely http. We'll use same strings as expected in existing tests.

Thus:

V7 = "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"
V4 = "http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#"
V6 = "http://json-schema.org/draft-06/schema#"
V201909 = "http://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/schema#"
V202012 = "http://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema#"

Ok.

Now craft cases.

MultipleDraftSubstrings:

id = "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/draft-04/schema#" -> expected V7.

OverlappingDraftPatterns:

- id = "http://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/draft-04/schema#" -> expected V201909.
- id = "http://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/draft-07/schema#" -> expected V202012? Wait order: 07 first, but 07 appears after 2020-12? Actually string contains "/draft-07/" after "/draft/2020-12/". The method checks contains "/draft-07/" first; it will find it regardless of position. So expected V7. Let's include that.

- id = "http://json-schema.org/draft-04/draft-06/schema#" -> expected V4 (since 04 before 06).

NonMatchingDraftPattern:

- id = "http://json-schema.org/draft07/schema#" -> unchanged (no slash before 07). Expected same.

- id = "http://json-schema.org/draft-07schema#" -> unchanged.

CaseSensitivity:

- id = "http://JSON-SCHEMA.ORG/draft-07/schema#" -> unchanged.

- id = "HTTP://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#" -> unchanged because contains "://json-schema.org/draft"? Actually contains "://json-schema.org/draft"? The string is "HTTP://...", case-sensitive, so "://json-schema.org/draft" not found due to "HTTP://". So unchanged.

EmptyString:

- id = "" -> expected "".

NullInput:

- id = null -> expected NullPointerException.

Ok.

Now format JSON. Use double quotes. Ensure each case input list includes parameter name "id". For null, value null (no quotes). Provide description.

Let's craft.
